name: Cathedral Basilica of the Assumption
history: Covington's first parish, St. Mary's, was dedicated in 1834 and became the cathedral when the diocese was formed in 1853. Bishop Camillus Paul Maes laid the cornerstone of the new cathedral in 1895 and dedicated it in 1901. The Madison Avenue facade was added in 1908-1910. Pius XII made it a basilica on 8 December 1953.
arch: French Gothic Revival: Leon Coquard drew on Notre-Dame de Paris, and the facade by David Davis followed. The towers were never carried to their planned height.
features: Its north transept window, 67 by 24 feet, made by Mayer of Munich in 1911, is one of the largest stained glass windows in the world.
Murals inside are by the American painter Frank Duveneck.

look.d: A Paris-style rose over three deep portals.
The towers stop square, like Notre-Dame's.

fun: For lack of funds, it opened in 1901 with no stained glass at all.
journal: Notre-Dame's echo on the Ohio River, with a window 67 feet tall.

quiz.q: How tall is the great transept window?
